sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Clermont-Ferrand has been making on-street parking easier to pay for while reopening some roads to cars that had been closed to them. Since 1 July 2026 the first 30 minutes in every paid zone are free, once per day per vehicle, when the driver pays through the PayByPhone app, which replaced PrestoPark on the same date [0][1]. As shown on the city page, the grid is 1.60 euros an hour in the violet zone, 1.20 in orange, 0.90 in green and 0.50 for the first hour in azure, and the post-parking charge is 30 euros, in force since 1 January 2023 [2]. Since 1 January 2024 residents of the paid zone have an annual resident subscription, one per household, that replaced the smart card and the daily resident rate [3].

Access to the centre has been reversed more than once. In October 2025 a central east-west axis was reported to reopen as a limited-traffic zone open to buses, residents, permit holders and cyclists, ahead of the new tram-bus lines B and C [5]; we found no confirmation that the zone is still in force in 2026. In summer 2026 the city said the avenues Raymond-Bergougnan, Carnot and Libération had been reopened to car traffic, and that after a consultation on 1 and 2 July the mayor had decided to reopen rue de l'Oradou to cars in both directions from 21 August 2026 [4]. The low-emission zone covers all 21 communes and bars unclassified professional goods vehicles, while private cars only need a Crit'Air sticker [14][15].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The park-and-ride network has been enlarged. The Le Brézet site opened on 2 February 2026 with 286 spaces on four levels, free to use, 17 minutes from the centre on line B [8], and La Pardieu Cristal opened on 15 April 2026 with 194 spaces. The Métropole says park-and-ride capacity has grown from 1,400 places on five sites in 2023 to 3,300 on 29 sites [9], and its parking page says the sites are currently free and that until early 2027 the exit barriers lift without a transport ticket being shown [10].

In the centre, the Vercingétorix car park on place de Jaude had its entrance and exit reversed in 2025, with the entrance on rue Lamartine and the exit on boulevard Desaix [6]. On 8 October 2026 the city told ICI that hourly entries had fallen in a series of records from September 2025, by as much as 53%, which it blamed on the reversal; it announced that entry would again be in front of the opera, with three weeks of works from 12 October and reopening planned for 31 October 2026 [7]. Parking at the Gabriel-Montpied hospital became paid on 6 July 2026, with 550 visitor spaces [17]. Public charging points run by the county energy body were inaugurated in 2022, 11 of them in Clermont-Ferrand [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The Métropole's parking page lists eight city-centre car parks run by SAGS, the largest being Gambetta (484 places) and Blaise Pascal (470) [11]. At Blaise Pascal a daytime stay costs 1.00 euro for 15 minutes, 1.50 for one hour and 7.00 for five hours, with 14.70 euros for 24 hours [12]. The open-data portal publishes an occupancy feed for barrier car parks, updated about every minute and credited to SAGS, Indigo and Effia, of which two park-and-ride entries have been invalid since April 2025 [13].

Our data cover 11 car parks with 2,598 spaces from that feed, measured since 5 October 2026. Occupancy averaged about 41% on weekdays and 41% at weekends, weighted by spaces, but the figures split into two kinds. The Cathédrale (292 spaces) and Saint-Pierre (167) are the fullest at 67% and 63% on weekdays, and both reached full in single readings. Blaise Pascal's underground garage (397) averaged 59%, Gambetta's surface car park (265) 60% on weekdays and 39% at weekends. By contrast the car parks tied to markets and weekends swing the other way: 1er Mai (266) averaged 34% on weekdays and 66% at weekends, and Les Pistes (400) 23% and 44%. The Vercingétorix car park (262 spaces in the feed) averaged only 19%, consistent with the city's statement of falling entries [7]. The Médiathèque garage is the quietest at 14% on weekdays and 3% at weekends. These are about two weeks of data.
